correctness.rationale: The semigroup is contractive in the Euclidean norm iff the symmetric Jacobian part is negative semidefinite; positivity implies a strictly growing infinitesimal vector. At balanced feedback, the signed cyclic shift is normal and has two-dimensional top symmetric eigenspace with exactly calculated compression slopes of opposite signs. A tridiagonal-path Schur complement derives both Chebyshev feedback endpoints, including equality cases; characteristic roots prove the stable-but-reactive rescue interval. A standalone script passes exact and independent numerical finite checks; no infinite conclusion is drawn solely from computation.

evidence: The equal-damping stability condition of Arcak and Sontag already implies the closed-loop characteristic stability threshold, so that part is explicitly not asserted novel.
Theorem 1 here adds the exact two-sided interval in b that makes J+J-transpose nonpositive and establishes strict minimization at b=a.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known stability does not imply contraction in a fixed Euclidean metric (stable nonnormal matrices can initially grow). A diagonal Lyapunov metric may differ from the identity and therefore does not dominate a fixed-metric no-amplification theorem. The statement is a new necessary-and-sufficient performance classification, with the recognized existing eigenvalue formula used only to distinguish the phases.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A possible equivalence is the negative cyclic-feedback secant criterion. That criterion tests whether some positive diagonal metric certifies stability and already gives the equal-damping Hurwitz bound. It does not imply that the identity metric works, determine a full exact interval in the closing coefficient for Euclidean contractivity, or assert uniqueness of the reactivity minimizer. The new statement deliberately excludes priority claims for the pre-existing spectral formula.

value.rationale: A complete, natural, all-length classification of feedback strengths preventing any norm amplification is biologically motivated by transient ecological responses, beyond a stability criterion. The exact gain interval and unique best instantaneous-growth rate distinguish two preservation goals and give a reproducible benchmark, with the motivating balanced-feedback rescue window. No empirical or nonlinear claims are made.
